newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa says chairman's health fine.
newsitem.headline: Televisa says chairman's health fine.

text.p: Emilio Azcarraga, the chairman of Mexican media conglomerate Grupo Televisa SA, was resting in his Los Angeles home and was not seriously ill, a company official told Reuters on Friday.

Manuel Alonso, president of news at Televisa, said Azcarraga had medical tests done on his heart but added that as far as he knew, Azcarraga had not suffered a heart attack. Televisa is the Spanish-speaking world's largest media company and the dominant broadcaster in Mexico.
"His health is fine. We spoke earlier in the day with him, he sounded in good spirits and gave us a few instructions about work," Alonso said in a telephone interview.
"His doctors have told him he is overworked and too tired, and he plans to rest in Los Angeles for a few weeks before returning to Mexico," Alonso said.

Televisa said on Thursday that Azcrraga, known as "The Tiger," was in Los Angeles for medical tests, prompting speculation the hugely influential chairman was gravely sick. Televisa's stock price fell both on Thursday and Friday on worries the company might be left without him. Its ADRs closed down $1 to 25-5/8 on Friday.

Alonso said Azcrraga would stay on at the helm of Televisa, but was unlikely to resume his full work load after returning to Mexico -- ceding additional responsibility to his son, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Emilio Azcrraga Jaen and Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Guillermo Caedo White.

"He will have to cut down on his work load...but this is a big institution, with 20,000 people, and we work here like a Swiss clock. We have ambitious growth plans and are not slowing down at all," Alonso said.

During Azcrraga's absence "some of the important decisions will be taken by Azcarraga Jaen and Caedo White. They will have the same posts, but with increased responsibility. When Mr. Azcarraga returns this will continue to some extent, although obviously less so."

Alonso said the company had been in touch with its major stockholders and had received full support from them. He said the decline in stock price in recent days was coincidental with a fall in the price of other Mexican stocks.
